problemStatement.formal: Define Stein's binaryGcd on natural numbers and prove binaryGcd a b = Nat.gcd a b for all a b.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize Stein's binary GCD algorithm and prove that it computes the same greatest common divisor as Nat.gcd.
whyMatters: Binary gcd is the subtraction-and-shift variant used by practical integer libraries for large inputs.
The proof packages the local gcd identities needed to justify each recursive branch of the algorithm.
A verified executable binaryGcd gives later cost-model proofs a trustworthy correctness foundation.

proven: The file proves the subtraction and factor-removal lemmas used by Stein's algorithm (Lean: gcd_sub_right, gcd_mul_two_left, gcd_mul_two_right, gcd_two_mul).
The recursive binaryGcd function is defined for natural-number inputs with termination by a + b.
Correctness is proved for all inputs: binaryGcd a b = Nat.gcd a b (Lean: binaryGcd_eq_gcd).
Basic API corollaries include commutativity and zero-input simplifications (Lean: binaryGcd_comm, binaryGcd_zero_left, binaryGcd_zero_right).
The related Euclidean-domain file records gcd divisibility/characterization lemmas beyond the Nat-specific binaryGcd proof.
knownResults.goal: Expose the verified correctness proof for Stein's binary gcd algorithm and its supporting gcd lemmas.

insights: binaryGcd.induct provides functional induction matching recursive cases exactly
Coprimality of 2 with odd numbers (Nat.coprime_two_left) is the key lemma for even-odd reduction
gcd_odd_sub_half combines subtraction and halving: gcd((a-b)/2, b) = gcd(a,b) for odd a,b
All supporting lemmas were already proved - only the main correctness theorem needed induction
